findings.subject: docs/known-issues-c001-pilot-r3.md:1,19,30-36; docs/ACCEPTANCE.md:49,61-63
findings.summary: The substantive known-issues publication gap is fixed: the supplied r3 document describes all current source limitations. However, the document supplied to cover r4 still names only r3 in its title/scope history and its mechanical-waiver link points only to the failed r3 prepare. There is no explicit r4 scope marker or r4 known-issues file. This is an attribution/publication issue, not a source-match defect. Concrete repair: explicitly extend this document to c001-pilot-r4 and link accept/c001-pilot-r4/prepare.json, or publish docs/known-issues-c001-pilot-r4.md linking the shared issues, before publishing/finalizing r4.
findings.repair: Add an explicit r4 scope/waiver reference to the shared document, or an r4-specific known-issues entry linking it; leave prepared sources, acceptance records and sealed reviews unchanged.

qualifications: The two switch functions intentionally preserve undefined/uninitialized results for selectors outside 0..11, with ORIGINAL BUG comments. Fresh local CFG inspection confirms those original paths return incoming r4. No proof that valid callers cannot reach those paths, and no portable behavior guarantee, is claimed.

Flexible e[] fixes the one-element-tail representation; actual allocation bounds and valid-index preconditions are still unrecovered and the original unchecked access is retained, as published in the shared known-issues document. Pilot struct layouts remain partial and names are placeholders, consistent with each unit use rather than fully recovered game types.

C++ remains mechanically unchecked under the recorded r4 waiver. I manually checked all declarations against all other source units and the original wrapper/constructor dataflow, including readonly 24-byte config copying. Full Heap/Widget/WidgetConfig definitions, RTTI, exception ABI and interprocedural aliases are not recovered.
The shared known-issues document substantively covers r4 by assignment, but needs explicit r4 attribution and the current waiver reference before publication/finalization (minor F01).

Seven new sequential match.py runs independently reproduce all 17 complete extents / 1,096 bytes. All 90 prepared/receipt/interface/object/output hash comparisons match. The r4 records report two fresh full builds and 178 tests, 0 skipped, 0 failed modules; I rehashed stored artifacts but did not run whole builds or the suite, and did not rerun the known r3 failure.

Gate v1.2 G0 and its pre-prepare guard were read; r4 prepare records commit 843b1f0b21684bfbb80097d4899dedb866449668. No git command was run, so clean-tree/HEAD identity is inherited from prepare rather than independently re-queried.

Inherited harness limits remain: original-armlink/section ordering/veneers/unwind equivalence unproven; lower RomFS IVFC not traversed (whole-CCI pin covers supplied dump); Windows cross-host reproduction pending. No runtime, emulator, behavior or native-port acceptance. These seven self-contained units have no source includes; old transitive-header limitations do not affect this source set.

Independent OpenAI reviewer, never the integrator or author. This is not a uniformly cross-family certificate: five original units were OpenAI CompilerIdR2-authored, while pilot_a.c and pilot_b.c were Anthropic-integrator authored.

verification.original_inspection: Fresh C++ wrapper/constructor pointer and config-copy provenance; fresh switch local CFG paths for selectors 0..11,12,13,-1,0x7fffffff. No original bytes or disassembly emitted.
